fact_text: In April 2018 the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) told banks that bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies were not legal tender and that banks could not settle or facilitate crypto transactions.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What are SBP's New Rules on Crypto Transactions Through Banks? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-11)

fact_text: In April 2026 the SBP issued a new circular allowing banks to open accounts for regulated, licensed crypto trading platforms and to settle their authorised transactions.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What are SBP's New Rules on Crypto Transactions Through Banks? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-11)

fact_text: The Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (PVARA) regulates and supervises virtual asset businesses, a role the guest compared to SECP's oversight of other financial firms.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What are SBP's New Rules on Crypto Transactions Through Banks? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-11)

fact_text: Before the circular banks treated crypto as a no-go area; the circular lets them facilitate it for licensed exchanges and companies, not individual investors.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What are SBP's New Rules on Crypto Transactions Through Banks? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-11)

fact_text: A licensed exchange needs at minimum a no-objection certificate (NOC) from PVARA to open a client money account, and the full licence tiers had not been defined.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What are SBP's New Rules on Crypto Transactions Through Banks? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-11)

fact_text: The guest said Binance held a PVARA no-objection certificate, while its full licence was still being processed.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What are SBP's New Rules on Crypto Transactions Through Banks? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-11)

fact_text: A client money account holds customers' funds at a licensed exchange on their behalf; it is a different arrangement from a normal retail bank deposit account.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What are SBP's New Rules on Crypto Transactions Through Banks? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-11)

fact_text: FTX collapsed within 72 hours after it treated customer deposits as its own money, with no check on how they were used, the guest said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What are SBP's New Rules on Crypto Transactions Through Banks? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-11)

fact_text: The guest said the framework is designed so that if a licensed exchange fails, clients' money stays protected, similar to how bank deposits are insulated.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What are SBP's New Rules on Crypto Transactions Through Banks? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-11)

fact_text: A gap noted by the guest: if client money buys bitcoin on an exchange, the coins sit with that exchange, and conventional banks have no mechanism to hold crypto holdings.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What are SBP's New Rules on Crypto Transactions Through Banks? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-11)

fact_text: Buying bitcoin or other crypto in Pakistan first needs a US-dollar stablecoin such as USDT or USDC, which the guest said is usually paid for peer to peer.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What are SBP's New Rules on Crypto Transactions Through Banks? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-11)

fact_text: The guest said most Pakistani crypto trades settle peer to peer in cash or by bank transfer outside the regulated channel, so that volume sits outside the tax net.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What are SBP's New Rules on Crypto Transactions Through Banks? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-11)

fact_text: The circular keeps existing anti-money-laundering and counter-terror-financing rules unchanged and adds stricter crypto checks on licensing, verification and background screening.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What are SBP's New Rules on Crypto Transactions Through Banks? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-11)

fact_text: Bybit, a Dubai-based exchange, holds large USDT or crypto deposits above a set threshold and asks the depositor for proof of source and purpose, the guest said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What are SBP's New Rules on Crypto Transactions Through Banks? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-11)

fact_text: Exchanges are expected to screen each incoming blockchain deposit (such as TRC20) for the sender's identity, relationship, purpose, wallet blacklist status and country risk.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What are SBP's New Rules on Crypto Transactions Through Banks? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-11)

fact_text: Centralised exchanges verify customers before opening accounts, with proof of address, national ID, driving licence and a liveness check; decentralised exchanges have no central control.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What are SBP's New Rules on Crypto Transactions Through Banks? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-11)

fact_text: The guest said there was no clarity on whether crypto bought before the circular could be traded through a bank client account, or how its gains would be taxed.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What are SBP's New Rules on Crypto Transactions Through Banks? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-11)

fact_text: The guest expected crypto profits to be taxed on sale like capital gains on stocks, but said no clarification had been issued for Binance holdings.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What are SBP's New Rules on Crypto Transactions Through Banks? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-11)

fact_text: The circular set no implementation timeline; the guest said the tax authority (FBR) would need its own rules and tax brackets, which could take some months.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What are SBP's New Rules on Crypto Transactions Through Banks? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-11)

fact_text: The guest said the controls could attract foreign investors into Pakistan's crypto sector.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What are SBP's New Rules on Crypto Transactions Through Banks? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-11)
